column1:
Information since March points to a strong labor market and solid growth, with inflation running below the symmetric 2% objective. The Committee held the target range at 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent and emphasized patience; the IOER tweak is a technical step to keep the funds rate within the target band rather than a stance change. In New Keynesian terms (Clarida, Galí, Gertler), anchored expectations alongside below-target inflation support a modest easing bias in guidance.

Financial Stability Report context (May 2019) tempers the tone: Equity market volatility had eased from late-2018 highs, funding risks remained low, and banks were well capitalized, but asset valuations were somewhat elevated and business-sector leverage (including leveraged loans/CLOs) was high. Overall vulnerabilities were moderate. These FSR insights support the Committee’s patient posture and argue against a more upbeat assessment despite solid activity.

Bottom line: Communication is mildly positive on growth and the labor market, but inflation undershoot and moderate financial stability vulnerabilities warrant caution.
